summary: Today, Grace Hill's point solutions (Training, Surveys, Policies, Mystery Shopping, Reputation Management, Intelligence+, Realync, HelloData®) are each priced and packaged on their own, with no shared PerformanceHQ commercial structure. Result: no ready-to-go package puts related solutions together, ~79% of GH-Success and ~50% of Mid-Market/Enterprise customers buy only one product, and there's no clear expansion path. The new structure organizes around the two workflows buyers actually own — Team Performance (L&D/Ops) and Property Performance (Marketing) — with PerformanceHQ as the connective data & intelligence layer across both, included as the foundation of every package, and a standardized per-unit commercial model. It is a three-decision purchase: (1) pick your workflow track(s), (2) pick your data & intelligence tier — PerformanceHQ (foundation, included) or PerformanceHQ Plus (+$0.59/unit/month upgrade), (3) add add-ons as needed. The Final deck's one-line version: know what matters, act on it, prove it worked — because keeping a resident protects NOI (a move-out costs about $3,872 to turn the unit, plus lost rent), and most tools show what happened without saying what to do next.

discountFramework.recommended: Cross-track buyer (both tracks): 8%. Power user (all Plus): 10%. Replaces today's 0% / 5% / 8% by count-of-solutions ladder — every new package already has a bundled discount baked into its list price, so the old “buy a 2nd point solution, get 5% off” step goes away.

discountFramework.how: Standardized unit-count tiers; per-unit rate falls as the portfolio grows.
discountFramework.recommended: Same step-downs across every package: 1,000–3,999 = list; 4,000–9,999 = -10%; 10,000–19,999 = -17.5%; 20,000+ = -17.5%. Today the buckets and rates vary by point solution (lowest: Training, highest: Policies) — this standardizes them.

Proposed in the Sept 16 working session as a new 10% discount for 3+ year terms, standard annual price increases still apply. CONTESTED IN THE ROOM (Sept 16): Sales leadership (Ashlee Horn) pushed back hard on making a multi-year discount standard — 56% of this quarter's contracts sold multi-year with no discount offered, and giving away margin by default risks eating into deal size given packages are already bundled/discounted. RML (Navi) agreed to take it offline and revisit an alternative: 3-year term as the standard list price, with a modest premium for a more flexible 1- or 2-year term, rather than a discount for going long. The Final deck (Sept 2026) does not resolve this — it covers naming, packaging and the pilot plan, not discount mechanics. Do not present the 10%-for-3-years figure as settled until this is resolved.

problemFirstMessaging.howToUse: Outside-in, VBF order (Value → Benefit → Feature) per Grace Hill's messaging framework: open with the problem/outcome the buyer already cares about, then the benefit, then how Grace Hill delivers it — the package and its features come last, as the mechanism, not the headline. corePitch above is the master four-line version of this; the per-track detail below is the expanded version for each buyer.

tracks.problem: Your team's execution is inconsistent from property to property, compliance risk sits on whoever happens to be on shift, and you can't tell whether that's a training gap, a policy gap, or a people problem until something has already gone wrong.
tracks.outcome: People performance: every employee, at every property, working to the same standard — fewer compliance incidents, faster onboarding, and execution that doesn't depend on your one strong regional manager.
tracks.benefit: You get ahead of the audit or the incident instead of reacting to it, and you can prove — not just hope — that your team is trained, policy-acknowledged, and performing to standard.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Training, policies, and mystery shopping working together under PerformanceHQ — industry-specific courseware, policy acknowledgment tracking, and on-site performance verification — packaged as Compliance, Core, or Plus depending on how far past baseline compliance you need to go.
tracks.proof: 64% of positive resident reviews mention the onsite team; one new hire costs about $4,700; 500,000+ multifamily professionals trained at 2,800+ companies.

tracks.problem: You don't have a reliable read on how residents and prospects actually feel about your properties until they leave a bad review, don't renew, or don't tour — and by then it's too late to do anything but react.
tracks.outcome: Property performance: leasing and retention that improve because you catch sentiment and friction early — in the resident relationship and in the leasing funnel — instead of finding out from a lost renewal or a 2-star review.
tracks.benefit: Fewer surprises at renewal, a reputation that supports (instead of undercuts) your marketing spend, and a leasing experience that converts more of the tours you're already paying for.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Resident and prospect surveys, reputation management, and Realync's leasing video tools working off the same PerformanceHQ data layer — packaged as Feedback & Reputation, Virtual Leasing, or Plus depending on whether the bigger gap is sentiment, conversion, or both.
tracks.proof: 41% of negative reviews during unit turnover are about maintenance; a turn costs about $3,872; up to 20% higher renewal intent than the national average with more than one Grace Hill tool.

sharedLayer.problem: You're making decisions about your portfolio without knowing how you stack up against the market — rents, comps, competitive positioning — which means every pricing and positioning call is a guess.
sharedLayer.outcome: Confidence that your people-performance and property-performance decisions are grounded in real market data, not internal signals alone.
sharedLayer.howWeDeliverIt: HelloData®, included as HelloData® Lite in every PerformanceHQ package and available at full depth (HelloData® Complete) in PerformanceHQ Plus — or standalone for teams (e.g., acquisitions, investment) that only need market data, not the workflow tracks.

objectionHandling.a: Separate tools each show one piece. A package connects them, so one finding leads to the next step. Most orgs run 20+ vendors — teams spend 40+ hours a month just reconciling them manually. Grace Hill is large enough to be a full platform — 1 of 4-5, not 1 of 20+.
Every move-out costs about $3,872 plus lost rent. Waiting has a price.

objectionHandling.q: Why are you changing the way Grace Hill is packaged? How does this benefit me?
objectionHandling.a: We're simplifying how customers buy Grace Hill. Instead of buying related capabilities one product at a time, you start with the business need and a package built around it — fewer buying decisions and a clearer path to expand over time.

objectionHandling.q: Why should I choose Grace Hill instead of a competitor?
objectionHandling.a: Grace Hill brings together a breadth of multifamily capabilities that's hard to replicate with a single alternative. You solve more needs within one ecosystem, and the value multiplies as those capabilities work together through PerformanceHQ rather than across disconnected systems.

objectionHandling.q: Why should I consolidate more of my technology with Grace Hill?
objectionHandling.a: Consolidation simplifies your tech stack and unlocks the additional value of PerformanceHQ's Intelligence+ — training, policies, performance measurement, resident feedback, leasing and market signals informing one another instead of sitting in separate systems.

objectionHandling.q: I only need Training / Surveys / Realync. Why do I need to move to a broader package?
objectionHandling.a: You don't need to buy the entire Grace Hill ecosystem. Start with the narrowest standard package that solves the need you have today, then expand only when another use case becomes relevant. The packages themselves stay intact — this preserves focused entry points without recreating à-la-carte complexity.

objectionHandling.q: Do all of my properties have to be on the same package?
objectionHandling.a: No. We can match the package to the parts of your portfolio where it makes sense, rather than forcing every property into the same configuration. GH Success and lower Mid-Market stay on one standard configuration; for eligible larger portfolios, Guided Flexibility can apply different standard packages across defined property groups; true property-level customization is Bespoke/CPQ, reserved for strategic accounts.

objectionHandling.q: My unit count changes throughout the year. How do you account for that?
objectionHandling.a: Pricing adjusts with your portfolio — we reconcile unit counts monthly, so additions and removals are reflected as your portfolio changes rather than locking you to the unit count at signing. This is the same process Grace Hill uses today.

objectionHandling.q: What if I need more mystery shops, or want to allocate them differently across my portfolio?
objectionHandling.a: You have flexibility beyond what's included in the package. Core includes two shops a year and Plus includes quarterly, but you can change the shop type or increase the frequency based on your needs, and you can always purchase additional shops on demand, above what's in the package.

objectionHandling.q: I only want a one-year contract. Why do I have to commit to multiple years?
objectionHandling.a: You don't have to — one-year contracts remain available. NOTE: the exact multi-year incentive structure (discount-for-3-years vs. premium-for-flexibility) was still being resolved as of Sept 16 — see discountFramework.

objectionHandling.q: This is a big price increase. Why should I pay more?
objectionHandling.a: The new price reflects a broader set of capabilities than what you're buying today, not simply a higher price for the same product. We'll work with you to make sure the package matches the needs you actually have, and if the change is significant, we can help manage the transition over time.
